docs.title: lochan-eda documentation
docs.text:
lochan-eda is a Python toolkit for two closely related jobs:

  1. Explore a tabular dataset quickly with summaries, plots, missing-value analysis, and a PDF report.
  2. Prepare numerical and categorical features for machine-learning workflows with learned preprocessing.

The documentation is organized around the way you actually use the package, not around its source-code file tree.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Ready to use — copy-paste workflows for the common cases.
  • AutomatedEDA — automatic train/test preparation and preprocessing.
  • Profiler — inspect a dataset and access the analysis tools.
  • Numerical — numerical summaries, plots, and numerical preprocessing.
  • Categorical — categorical summaries, plots, and categorical preprocessing.
  • Missing — visualize missing values.
  • Report — generate a PDF EDA report.

docs.title: Package API
docs.text:
The package currently exposes these classes from the top-level namespace:

from lochan_eda import AutomatedEDA, Profiler, Numerical, Categorical

Missing and Report are used by Profiler but are not currently exported from lochan_eda.__init__.

docs.title: AutomatedEDA
docs.text:
AutomatedEDA is the high-level preprocessing interface. It separates numerical and categorical columns, learns preprocessing rules from training data, and applies those rules to transformed data.

from lochan_eda import AutomatedEDA

eda = AutomatedEDA()

docs.title: prepare()
docs.text:
eda.prepare(
    X,
    target=None,
    exclude=None,
    split=True,
    test_size=0.2,
    random_state=42,
    stratify=None,
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description X pd.DataFrame required Feature DataFrame, or a DataFrame containing the target column. target str \| pd.Series \| None None Target column name or an independent target Series. exclude list None Columns to leave out of preprocessing. split bool True Whether to create train/test splits. test_size float 0.2 Fraction assigned to the test set when splitting. random_state int 42 Random state passed to train_test_split. stratify array-like None Stratification values passed to train_test_split when a target is present.

docs.title: Return shapes
docs.text:
The return value depends on target and split:

target split Returns None False X None True X_train, X_test provided False X, y provided True X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test

docs.title: Typical use
docs.text:
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = eda.prepare(
    df,
    target="target",
    test_size=0.2,
    random_state=42,
)

docs.title: fit()
docs.text:
eda.fit(X, y=None)

Learns preprocessing rules separately for numerical and categorical columns.

fit() returns None.

docs.title: transform()
docs.text:
X_processed = eda.transform(X)

With a target:

X_processed, y = eda.transform(X, y)

The method applies the rules learned by fit().

docs.title: Numerical data
docs.text:
Numerical can learn rules for:

  • columns with high missingness
  • missing-value imputation
  • outlier treatment
  • scaling
  • logarithmic transformation for strongly right-skewed non-negative features

docs.title: Categorical data
docs.text:
Categorical can learn rules for:

  • columns with high missingness
  • missing-value imputation
  • rare-category grouping
  • binary encoding
  • one-hot encoding
  • frequency encoding

The exact rule is learned from the training data and reused during transformation.

docs.title: Categorical
docs.text:
Categorical provides categorical EDA and categorical preprocessing.

from lochan_eda import Categorical

categorical = Categorical(profiler_df=df)

In normal exploratory workflows, use it through Profiler:

profile.categorical

docs.title: summary()
docs.text:
summary = profile.categorical.summary()

Returns DataFrame.describe() output for object, category, and string columns.

If there are no categorical columns, an empty DataFrame is returned.

docs.title: plot(columns=None, top_n=10)
docs.text:
profile.categorical.plot()

Select specific categorical columns:

profile.categorical.plot(
    columns=["city", "segment"],
    top_n=8,
)

Categories beyond top_n are grouped as Others in the plot.

The figure is saved as categorical_plots.png.

docs.title: fit(data, exclude=None)
docs.text:
categorical.fit(X_train)

Learns missing-value, rare-category, and encoding rules from the training data.

docs.title: transform(data, exclude=None)
docs.text:
X_processed = categorical.transform(X_test)

Applies the rules learned during fit().

docs.title: imputer(learn=False)
docs.text: Learns which highly-missing categorical columns should be dropped and which missing values should be filled.

docs.title: rare_manager(learn=False)
docs.text: Learns low-frequency categories and groups them into Other during transformation.

docs.title: encoder(learn=False)
docs.text:
Chooses an encoding strategy from the number of unique values:

  • Binary for up to 2 unique values
  • One-hot for up to 10 unique values
  • Frequency encoding above 10 unique values

docs.title: Missing
docs.text:
Missing provides a focused visualization of missing values across columns.

It is normally accessed through Profiler:

from lochan_eda import Profiler

profile = Profiler(df)
profile.missing.plot()

docs.title: plot()
docs.text:
fig = profile.missing.plot()

The plot shows each column's percentage of missing values, ordered from lower to higher missingness in the chart.

The figure is saved as:

missing_plot.png

If the DataFrame is empty, the method returns None. If there are no missing values, the returned figure displays No Missing Value Found.

docs.title: Numerical
docs.text:
Numerical provides numerical EDA and numerical preprocessing.

from lochan_eda import Numerical

numerical = Numerical(profiler_df=df)

In normal exploratory workflows, use it through Profiler:

profile.numerical

docs.title: summary()
docs.text:
summary = profile.numerical.summary()

Returns a DataFrame from numerical describe() output with additional columns for:

  • standard deviation
  • missing-value percentage
  • skew
  • zero percentage
  • outlier percentage

If there are no numerical columns, an empty DataFrame is returned.

docs.title: plot(columns=None)
docs.text:
profile.numerical.plot()

Restrict the plot to selected numerical columns:

profile.numerical.plot(columns=["age", "income"])

For each selected column the figure contains:

  1. Distribution histogram
  2. Box plot
  3. Normal Q-Q plot

The figure is also saved as numerical_plots.png.

docs.title: fit(data, exclude=None)
docs.text:
numerical.fit(X_train)

Learns numerical preprocessing rules from the supplied training DataFrame.

docs.title: transform(data, exclude=None)
docs.text:
X_processed = numerical.transform(X_test)

Applies the learned preprocessing rules. fit() must be called first.

docs.title: imputer(learn=False)
docs.text: Internal preprocessing stage for missing numerical values. During learning it determines columns to drop and values used for imputation.

docs.title: outlier_manager(learn=False)
docs.text: Internal preprocessing stage for outlier handling. Depending on learned data behavior, it can learn clipping, square-root, or log1p transformations.

docs.title: scaler(learn=False)
docs.text: Internal preprocessing stage for feature scaling. The implementation can select MaxAbsScaler, StandardScaler, or RobustScaler, and can learn a log1p transformation for strongly right-skewed non-negative data.

docs.title: Profiler
docs.text:
Profiler is the main entry point for exploratory analysis.

from lochan_eda import Profiler

profile = Profiler(df, target="target")

If target is a column name, that column is separated from the DataFrame used by the profiler.

The profiler exposes:

profile.numerical
profile.categorical
profile.missing
profile.report

docs.title: overview()
docs.text:
result = profile.overview()

Prints and returns dataset-level statistics.

The returned dictionary contains:

rows
columns
memory_usage
duplicate_rows
duplicate_percentage
missing_cells
missing_percentage
numerical_columns
categorical_columns
datetime_columns

Example:

overview = profile.overview()
print(overview["missing_percentage"])

docs.title: Ready to use
docs.text: This page is the shortest path from installation to useful output.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: pip install lochan-eda

docs.title: 1. Prepare a dataset for machine learning
docs.text:
For a DataFrame with a target column:

from lochan_eda import AutomatedEDA

eda = AutomatedEDA()

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = eda.prepare(
    df,
    target="target"
)

By default, prepare() performs an 80/20 train-test split and learns preprocessing from the training data before transforming both splits.

docs.title: Keep a column untouched
docs.text:
Use exclude for columns that should not be processed:

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = eda.prepare(
    df,
    target="target",
    exclude=["customer_id"]
)

docs.title: Use a separate target Series
docs.text:
y = df["target"]
X = df.drop(columns="target")

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = eda.prepare(
    X,
    target=y
)

docs.title: Do not split
docs.text:
X_processed, y = eda.prepare(
    df,
    target="target",
    split=False
)

If there is no target:

X_processed = eda.prepare(
    df,
    split=False
)

docs.title: 2. Profile a dataset
docs.text:
from lochan_eda import Profiler

profile = Profiler(df, target="target")

Get a high-level overview:

profile.overview()

docs.title: 3. Inspect numerical columns
docs.text:
profile.numerical.summary()
profile.numerical.plot()

The numerical plot contains a distribution, box plot, and Q-Q plot for each numerical column.

docs.title: 4. Inspect categorical columns
docs.text:
profile.categorical.summary()
profile.categorical.plot()

To limit the number of categories shown per column:

profile.categorical.plot(top_n=10)

docs.title: 5. Inspect missing values
docs.text:
profile.missing.plot()

The plot is saved as missing_plot.png in the current working directory.

docs.title: 6. Generate a PDF report
docs.text:
profile.report.save("report.pdf")

The report contains a dataset overview and the report components implemented by the package.

docs.title: A practical first workflow
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from lochan_eda import Profiler, AutomatedEDA

# Load
 df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")

# Explore
profile = Profiler(df, target="target")
profile.overview()
profile.numerical.summary()
profile.categorical.summary()
profile.missing.plot()
profile.report.save("eda_report.pdf")

# Prepare
eda = AutomatedEDA()
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = eda.prepare(
    df,
    target="target"
)

docs.title: Report
docs.text:
Report generates a PDF report from a Profiler instance.

It is normally accessed as:

from lochan_eda import Profiler

profile = Profiler(df)
profile.report.save("report.pdf")

docs.title: save(filepath="report.pdf")
docs.text: profile.report.save("eda_report.pdf")

docs.title: Parameter
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description filepath str report.pdf Path where the PDF report is written.

The generated report contains the dataset overview and the report sections implemented by the current Report class.

The PDF is built with ReportLab and includes a consistent header, footer, page numbering, and tabular presentation of overview information.
